cells.tense: Clear sight is arriving now, and you are the one holding the pen.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: Follow this week's sharpest notice one step past where you'd rather stop, and sit in that step a minute. Nothing has to come of it.
cells.core:
You can catch a thing plainly before you know what it means, and that catching is the whole skill here — knowing what to attend to without needing to explain it first. In a good stretch the noticed thing opens and keeps opening, and the work follows what you saw instead of chasing it. Nothing analytical drives that. The attention does it.

What holds it back is stopping where the thought gets uncomfortable. Follow the sharpest thing you noticed this week one step further — the part you'd rather not think through — and sit there a minute. Going all the way into the pattern is where the depth comes from, not stepping back to survey it. There's no finish line and no conclusion you owe anyone. Don't stop early, and the shape rounds itself out in time.
cells.sheetLine: You see it plainly. Stay with it one step longer.
cells.verb: seeing a thing plainly before you know what it means
cells.place: the moment before you decide what deserves your attention

cells.tense: You are bracing for a clarity that has already arrived, out ahead of it.
cells.act: carry what the spark became to its full size
cells.ask: Whatever you saw recently is being handled like a fragment. Let it get all the way to what it actually is, whole, and hold that before you act.
cells.core:
Something has shown up clearly, and you are already several turns into what it will mean. That's the excess — treating each fresh look as a finished conclusion, planning around a picture that hasn't finished forming. Your attention is sharp and it's spent on the next turn instead of the one you're standing in. At ease, this works as radiance without ego: you shine because it's what you do, not to prove anything.

The repair is presence, not more cutting. Let what you saw get all the way to what it actually is, whole, and hold that before you act on it. Not early, not ahead. Holding it at full size lets the picture arrive before you spend it. Staying with it is the work, not looking harder.
cells.sheetLine: You're ahead of what you saw. Let it finish arriving.
cells.verb: seeing a thing plainly before you know what it means
cells.place: the moment before you decide what deserves your attention

cells.tense: You understood something, and you are still standing at the threshold you passed.
cells.act: complete the form so it stands without you
cells.ask: Take what you understood but stopped building past. Finish only the first piece today, so it holds up with nobody's hand on it.
cells.core:
The realization came. It is real, and nothing got built on it — the insight sits in the doorway and the form it called for was not made. Attention goes to reviewing what was understood rather than to what it asked for, and the hours that could carry it forward go to standing still. What this needs is not more looking. Looking is present; completion isn't.

What charges this is direction, not feeling. Take what you understood but stopped building past, and finish only the first piece — small enough for today — so it holds up with nobody's hand on it. Not the whole thing, one piece standing. When one piece stands, the next becomes visible, and attention comes back up by doing rather than by waiting to feel ready.
cells.sheetLine: You understood. Something still needs to stand.

cells.tense: Insight moves through your day and it gets filed as how the day was.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: When the next clear thing comes into view, note once that you saw it, then meet it as it is before deciding what it's for.
cells.core:
Something keeps getting seen — the pattern under the pattern, the person's real question — and your account of it has you standing there when it shows up, as if anyone would have seen the same. At the moment it comes, before you decide what it's for, you are doing something no one else is doing. The turning is not a thing that waits for you at the end of a thought. It is where you already are.

Meet what is arriving as it arrives. The next clear thing you see, note once that you saw it, then meet it as it is, before deciding what it's for. Each moment comes in fresh rather than as more of the last. Claiming the moment of noticing is the whole correction — nothing grander is being asked for.
cells.sheetLine: You saw it. Note the moment, then meet the next.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's seeing 'hasn't cut anything yet' — the record says the signature is the first cut of clarity arising, but I can't know from a card whether they have or haven't acted on what they've seen. A reader could reasonably say 'I've been cutting for years, I just can't stop.' The ask survives being wrong because following one thought to its edge is useful whether perception is new or old. The sentence that serves me more than them: any framing that makes the dawning sound pristine or special — that flatters the card, not the person.
